dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agencies (USGS and State Department), U.S. and allied private-sector mining and resource companies, and partner foreign countries.
dimensions.evidence: private companies headquartered in the United States or an allied foreign country are offered the right of first refusal

dimensions.assessment: Facilitates international scientific cooperation, private sector investment, and supply chain security for critical minerals without imposing domestic regulatory mandates.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary may enter into a memorandum of understanding with 1 or more heads of agencies of partner foreign countries with respect to scientific and technical cooperation

dimensions.assessment: Requires cost estimation and reporting for each MOU entered into, potentially leveraging financing entities like the DFC and Ex-Im Bank, but does not specify a lump-sum appropriation.
dimensions.evidence: submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a report detailing the implementing partners, scope of the memorandum of understanding, activities to be undertaken, estimated costs, and source of funding.

dimensions.assessment: Grants specific statutory authorization for international scientific MOUs, interagency coordination with the State Department, and congressional reporting.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary may enter into a memorandum of understanding with 1 or more heads of agencies of partner foreign countries

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes ongoing international cooperative agreements and continuous congressional reporting and oversight mechanisms.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 30 days before the Secretary intends to enter into a memorandum of understanding under subsection (a), the Secretary shall notify...

missing_information: Specific countries targeted for initial partnership agreements.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill authorizes the U.S. Geological Survey to enter into memoranda of understanding with partner foreign countries to map critical minerals and rare earth elements, subject to state department concurrence, congressional notification, and data protection requirements.
